# getfileattr

Returns the attributes of a file or directory. *(version 4.69 or later)*

```ttl
getfileattr <filename>
```

## Parameters

**string &lt;filename&gt;**

The file name or directory name

## Return Value

**System variable &lt;result&gt;**

When this command fails, -1 is stored.
When the command succeeds, the returned value is in the following:
Value Meaning $1 Read only $2 Hidden $4 The operating system uses a part of, or uses exclusively $10 Directory $20 Archive $80 Not have other attributes set $100 Temporary $200 Sparse file $400 Has an associated reparse point, or a file that is a symbolic link $800 Compressed $1000 Physically moved to offline storage(Windows 2000 or later) $2000 Not to be indexed by the content indexing service(Windows 2000 or later) $4000 Encrypted

## Example

```ttl
file = 'c:\test.txt'
getfileattr file
if result <> -1 then
	if result & $1 > 0 then
		messagebox 'This file has readonly attribute.' file
	endif
endif
```

```ttl
name = "C:\test"

getfileattr name

if result < 0 then
	messagebox "Not found" name
elseif result & $10 then
	messagebox "Directory" name
else
	messagebox "File" name
endif
```
